decisions.reason: Clause 2 allowed unrelated probability spaces and did not specify a joint reference law, whereas def-cm-calibration-rule clause 4 requires either all fixed bounded inputs or one joint Borel deviation vector. Repaired with those two branches; mixed inputs use constant components in the joint branch, without independence. Normalized coordinates identify the deviation norm with the supplier Euclidean norm. Realized calibration still requires no measurability of Gamma; random calibration retains its separate measurability/domain hypotheses.

The arbitrary readout in def-cm18-observable-model permits R identically zero, so Phi is identical in both frames despite transformed times and states. Replaced the false categorical change with the requirement to transform the protocol/readout and compute its new prediction; invariant numerical readouts remain admitted. Galilean signs t prime=t+b and x prime=Rx+vt+a and the conditional force-domain convention are preserved. No item cites this remark; the owning page only records frame relativity and remains sound.

def-cm-confidence-set-and-coverage defines a level as a uniform lower bound on coverage, not necessarily the infimum itself. A family with infimum coverage 0.97 also has declared level 0.95, contradicting the original equality wording. Repaired with the exact measurable-event definition and infimum >= 1-alpha condition; no parameter probability is introduced. Reviewed the calibrated-reference use after the joint-law repair: this item assumes no separate reference spaces. The finite-sample consumer uses only the specified-test ingredients, so its proof and claim remain sound.

The rejected identification is absent: clause 5 lists evaluation methods for the source and calibration, without assigning statistical uncertainty to Type A or systematic uncertainty to Type B. GUM 0.7 separates evaluation method from random/systematic effects, while 4.2 and 4.3.1 support the listed repeated-observation and other-information methods. The item requires source-backed uncertainty and carried input qualifications, reports no measurements, and remains compatible with both methods for either effect. Its calibration use remains sound after the joint-law repair; no actual datum is instantiated.

Confirmed a nonfatal supplier-restatement defect in L4: integrability of R and its mean bound need a finite second centered moment; the variance comparison needs a finite fourth moment. L4 now states C2 regularity, mu in the convex domain and both moment conditions exactly. The actual example already has square-integrable X in a bounded positive box, giving E|X-mu|^4 <= (rho_l^2+rho_T^2)^2, so its mean, Hessian, covariance and variance-error conclusions and all Verification steps remain valid. The Example and physical_scope are unchanged; contract derivations and supplier-section quotes remain exact. Calibration is only a future requirement, not an instantiated datum.

The force branch accepts prescribed regular force data; prescribed E and B maps need no source equations or boundary/radiation model. Thus the original universal requirement excluded admissible external-field couplings, for example constant E and zero B on all space. Repaired clause 2 with exact field-map domains in a named frame, declared component units and regularity, a prescribed-data branch and a separately solved field-model branch. The total force still must satisfy continuity and state-local Lipschitz hypotheses; singular/distributional cases are qualified. No electromagnetic equation or conservation theorem is imported. No item directly uses this remark; the page summarizes charge, fields and a coupling law and stays sound.

The finite-time supplier bounds the Euclidean norm, whereas the residual/readout lemma allows any metric. On the same set the metric d(u,v)=sqrt(||u-v||) need not satisfy d(u,v)<=||u-v||, so the original combined bound does not follow. Repaired by requiring y_j in the common phase-state set and either the same Euclidean metric or an explicit finite comparison d<=c_d||. Then d(x_n,y_n)<=I_n+c_d D_n and the readout bound follows with Lambda. Map Lipschitz L_map remains distinct from exact-field L; positive step, stage definedness, retention, analytic hypotheses and empirical separation remain intact. The owning page uses only the separate certified estimates and remains sound.

Verified the Step-4 concern in current Definition conventions: categorical independence failure for a shared systematic effect is false. For n>=2, epsilon_k=b+U_k with fixed bias b and mutually independent identically distributed Bernoulli U_k stays IID; changing preparation need not change a law, and reused deterministic readings stay independent. The adopted-IID bounds themselves remain conditional and sound. Route this draft frontier item to its ordinary owner; unit 34 has no rejected tuple or write authority for it.
ledger_updates.affected_use: Independence of the errors fails when successive repetitions share a systematic effect ... identical distribution fails when the preparation or the conditions change between repetitions.

ledger_updates.minimality: Replace only the categorical warning with conditions that can violate IID; retain the adopted hypotheses and sample-mean result.

ledger_updates.reason: The supplier Definition correctly uses inf gamma>=1-alpha, but its Well-definedness prose says the level is an infimum. That repeats the same false equality repaired in the assigned model-test remark; a set with infimum 0.97 also has declared level 0.95. The consuming repair uses the exact correct Definition. Route this draft supplier to its frontier owner and examine its direct references only if that public definition changes.

ledger_updates.invalidated_claim: A declared lower coverage level need not equal the coverage infimum.
ledger_updates.minimality: Change the convention paragraph to say uniform lower bound on pre-data coverage, preserving the Definition inequality.

ledger_updates.reason: Its Definition frame-relativity paragraph also says a change of frame changes the readout of the same protocol. Read literally as numerical change, this conflicts with the permitted constant readout R=0, as in the assigned Galilean-regime rejection. The protocol and states must be re-expressed, but the numerical readout may be invariant. No assigned deduction relies on a compulsory numerical change. Route this draft supplier to its frontier owner for the same precise qualification; do not infer any published defect.

ledger_updates.invalidated_claim: An arbitrary readout is not necessarily numerically altered by a frame change.
ledger_updates.minimality: Qualify the convention as transformation/re-expression according to the declared readout law; retain the protocol data and allowed invariant readouts.
